instruction: For this task, start with `/home/user/Desktop/blade_mode.fst` and its version-matched structural dependency closure. On this machine, the OpenFAST executable is `/home/user/miniconda3/bin/openfast` when working on `blade_mode.fst`. Complete a structural-only BeamDyn blade modal analysis from the command line: 1. Confirm `CompElast=2`, disable InflowWind, AeroDyn, and ServoDyn, enable `Linearize=True`, `NLinTimes=1`, and module linearization output. In ElastoDyn enable `FlapDOF1`, `FlapDOF2`, and `EdgeDOF`, while tower and drivetrain DOFs remain disabled. 2. Run `openfast blade_mode.fst` from `/home/user/Desktop` and retain its normal-termination log and newly generated `/home/user/Desktop/blade_mode.1.BD1.lin`. 3. Write `/home/user/Desktop/postprocess.py` to read the BD1 continuous-state A matrix, compute its eigenvalues, convert positive imaginary parts to Hz with `imag(lambda)/(2*pi)`, sort ascending, and report the first two structural blade modes as flap1 and edge1. For this structural-only v5 case the expected neighborhoods are approximately 0.740 Hz and 1.111 Hz. 4. Save `/home/user/Desktop/summary.txt` as `flap1_hz, edge1_hz`. 5. Do not use GUI tools. [Init Package Note] Only initialization inputs are preloaded; no frequency table or result artifact is supplied.
